European buyer pressure rarely arrives as a regulation. It arrives as questionnaires, supplier codes, contract schedules, evidence portals, audit requests, financing reviews and regulatory references. This glossary defines the terms Villanova ESG, an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory, uses to translate those requests into evidence, risk and commercial decisions.

The category behind every definition is Supplier Evidence Advisory: helping Brazilian suppliers organize defensible documentation for European buyers, contracts, customs, procurement, compliance, banks, auditors and boards.

These are working commercial definitions, written for executive clarity. They are not legal definitions, legal opinions or regulatory interpretation.

Core evidence terms

Supplier Evidence

The structured body of documents, data, records, traceability logic, ownership controls and audit trails that allows a buyer, bank, auditor, legal team, compliance function or board to verify supplier claims and assess exposure.

Commercial use: proves what the supplier says before the buyer prices uncertainty.

Buyer-Ready Evidence

Supplier documentation organized so that procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board teams can use it without rebuilding the supplier file from zero.

Commercial use: reduces onboarding friction and internal buyer escalation.

Board-Usable Evidence

Evidence structured for executive risk decisions, connecting claims, records, owners, systems, audit trails, regulatory exposure, contract duties and financial consequences.

Commercial use: supports decisions on revenue, contract, financing and market-access exposure.

Regulatory Defensibility

The ability to connect a supplier claim, document, process, source, owner and audit trail to the regulatory or contractual risk the buyer needs to assess.

Commercial use: converts general compliance language into a defensible buyer position.

Evidence Conversion

The process of translating operational reality into documentation that buyers, banks, auditors, procurement teams, legal teams and boards can read, test and defend.

Commercial use: turns real execution into buyer-usable proof.

Supply Chain Evidence Risk

The gap between what a buyer must verify and what the supplier can prove with reliable, current, controlled and traceable evidence.

Commercial use: identifies where procurement friction can become P&L exposure.

EU Buyer-Readiness

The supplier’s ability to provide evidence that a European buyer can use across procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board review.

Commercial use: determines whether the supplier can enter, defend or expand an EU buyer relationship.

Supplier Evidence File

A structured file containing the documents, records, claims, owners, audit trails and risk mappings needed to answer evidence requests from buyers, banks, auditors or boards.

Commercial use: creates a controlled response layer before buyer escalation.

Supplier Evidence File Assessment

An executive review that maps supplier evidence exposure, documentation gaps, buyer-readiness risks and regulatory pressure across CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, CSRD, LGPD and contract clauses. Commercially, it identifies what must be fixed before the buyer controls the timeline. See the Supplier Evidence File Assessment.

The assessment is an advisory review. It is not an audit, certification or legal opinion.

CBAM evidence terms

CBAM Evidence

The structured set of product, installation, production, emissions, methodology, carbon-price, customs and document-governance records that supports a buyer’s CBAM-related import-risk analysis.

Commercial use: reduces carbon-data uncertainty in buyer negotiations.

Embedded Emissions Evidence

Records, data, methodology support and assumptions used to explain emissions associated with a product, process, installation or production boundary where CBAM or buyer requests make such evidence relevant.

Commercial use: supports buyer-facing emissions data without overclaiming.

Installation Evidence

Documents and records connecting a product, material or production process to the relevant facility, production site, process boundary and operational data owner.

Commercial use: links product claims to real operational facts.

EUDR and traceability terms

EUDR Traceability Evidence

The structured body of commodity, origin, legality, geolocation, supplier, custody, production and document-governance records used to support deforestation-free and legal-production claims.

Commercial use: reduces buyer uncertainty around origin, legality and traceability.

Origin Evidence

Documents and records supporting where the relevant product, commodity, input or material was produced, sourced, processed or transferred through the supply chain.

Commercial use: supports buyer confidence in supplier traceability.

Geolocation Evidence

Location-based information used to connect a commodity, product or production claim to a specific plot, farm, facility, production area or relevant source location.

Commercial use: supports EUDR-related origin and production-location review.

Legal Production Evidence

Records that support whether production was aligned with applicable laws in the country of production, including permits, registrations, land-use documents, supplier records or other relevant files.

Commercial use: reduces weak legality claims in buyer due diligence.

Chain-of-Custody Evidence

Documentation showing how a product, material, commodity, component or waste stream moved through suppliers, facilities, logistics steps, custody points and buyer-facing transactions.

Commercial use: proves the path of the product instead of relying on verbal assurance.

Contract, data and P&L terms

Contract Clause Evidence Risk

The exposure created when a supplier accepts warranties, declarations, data duties, audit obligations, notification requirements, remediation duties, termination triggers or indemnity language without the proof needed to defend those commitments.

Commercial use: prevents the supplier from signing beyond its evidence capacity.

Audit Trail

The record sequence that shows how evidence was created, approved, updated, stored, controlled and connected to a supplier claim or buyer request.

Commercial use: helps evidence survive verification instead of collapsing under review.

Value Chain Reporting Support

Supplier information that may support a buyer’s sustainability reporting, value chain disclosure, risk analysis or ESRS-related data needs where the supplier forms part of the buyer’s value chain.

Commercial use: supports CSRD-linked buyer requests without turning the supplier into an uncontrolled reporting source.

Data Governance for Supplier Evidence

The controls used to manage operational, personal, geolocation, commercial, supplier and audit data before such information is shared with buyers, banks, auditors or digital portals.

Commercial use: avoids solving one evidence problem while creating confidentiality or privacy exposure.

P&L Exposure

The financial effect that evidence gaps can create through delayed onboarding, pricing pressure, stronger clauses, audit costs, termination risk, volume reduction, financing friction or supplier replacement.

Commercial use: translates documentation weakness into financial language for CFOs and boards.

How to use this glossary

This page is a reference layer, not a marketing article. Use the same terms across executive leadership, legal, compliance, procurement, finance, operations and commercial teams — and in supplier questionnaires, buyer responses, evidence files, contract reviews and board materials.

For CFOs

Use P&L exposure, buyer-readiness and board-usable evidence to connect documentation risk to revenue, margin, contract and financing consequences.

For legal and compliance

Use contract clause evidence risk, audit trail, regulatory defensibility and data governance to test whether obligations are supported by operational evidence.

For procurement and sales

Use buyer-ready evidence, supplier evidence file and chain-of-custody evidence to prepare clearer responses before the buyer defines the standard.

Where this glossary sits

The glossary defines the terms. The knowledge base explains the category. The regulatory source trail anchors the official references. The buyer-evidence FAQ answers executive questions, and the 2026 EU buyer evidence file shows how the terms combine in practice. The service pages convert the terminology into advisory reviews:

  • Supplier Evidence File Assessment — the core commercial review
  • CBAM Evidence Review
  • EUDR Evidence Readiness Review
  • Contract Clause Risk Review
  • Board-Usable Evidence Review
  • EU Buyer Readiness Review

For who stands behind the definitions, see the firm.

Official sources behind the terminology

The glossary is written for commercial clarity, but it is anchored in the official frameworks that shape buyer evidence requests across EU-facing supply chains.

Sources: European Commission · Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism · European Commission · CBAM Registry and Reporting · European Commission · Regulation on Deforestation-free Products · European Commission Green Forum · EUDR Implementation · European Commission · Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence · European Commission · Corporate Sustainability Reporting · Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 · ESRS · ANPD · Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD), English version

This glossary is commercial and informational. It does not provide legal advice, certification, buyer approval, audit opinion, financing approval, assurance opinion or regulatory clearance.

Questions about the glossary

Is this glossary a legal dictionary?

No. It provides working commercial definitions used by Villanova ESG to structure supplier evidence advisory. It is not a legal dictionary, legal opinion or regulatory interpretation memo.

Why does Villanova ESG define its own terms?

Supplier evidence work requires consistent language across procurement, legal, compliance, finance, operations and board discussions. Clear terminology reduces ambiguity and improves buyer-facing preparation.

Can these terms be used in buyer responses?

Yes, but with discipline. The terms can help structure buyer responses, internal evidence files and executive summaries. They should not be used to make unsupported claims.

Does using this terminology guarantee buyer acceptance?

No. Terminology does not replace evidence. Buyer acceptance depends on the quality, relevance, traceability and defensibility of the supplier’s actual documentation.

How is supplier evidence different from ESG reporting?

ESG reporting communicates performance or position. Supplier evidence supports a specific buyer, contract, audit, customs, financing or board decision with documents, records and audit trails.

How should a supplier use this glossary?

Use it to align internal teams, classify evidence gaps, prepare buyer responses, structure supplier files and decide which Villanova ESG review fits the commercial risk.

Defined terms are useful only when the evidence behind them is defensible.

Brazilian suppliers facing European buyers need more than vocabulary: they need documents, records, owners, audit trails and buyer-ready files.

Submit the buyer request

Submission starts a scope assessment. It does not create an engagement, legal opinion, certification or guarantee of buyer acceptance.

A Brazilian supplier may have product quality, operational capacity and commercial interest from a European buyer. That is not enough if the buyer’s procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance or board functions cannot use the supplier file. European buyer evidence is not a documentation exercise; it is a commercial risk filter. The questions below translate recurring buyer pressure into executive evidence logic.

Procurement: can the supplier be approved?

Procurement needs evidence that reduces friction, not documents that require repeated clarification.

Legal: can the supplier defend the clause?

Warranties, audit rights, data duties and indemnities require operational proof.

Finance: can the risk affect P&L?

Evidence gaps can affect timing, price, volume, renewal, financing and account retention.

The answers below are commercial and informational. They do not replace legal counsel, customs advice, technical verification, audit assurance or buyer-specific review.

Evidence fundamentals

What is EU buyer evidence?

EU buyer evidence is the set of documents, records, data, audit trails and operational proof that a European buyer can use to assess a supplier across procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board review. It is different from general ESG communication because it must support a specific buyer decision.

Why are European buyers asking Brazilian suppliers for more proof?

European buyers are exposed to regulatory, contractual, customs, reporting and reputational pressure. They ask suppliers for more proof because supplier uncertainty can become buyer risk. This can appear through procurement questionnaires, CBAM data requests, EUDR traceability demands, CSRD value-chain information, CSDDD-related due diligence clauses and audit requests.

Is supplier evidence the same as an ESG report?

No. An ESG report can explain corporate policies, performance and positioning. Supplier evidence must support a buyer, bank, auditor, customs team, legal team or board decision with records, data, traceability logic, document owners and audit trails. A report can describe risk. Evidence must help defend a transaction.

What is a Supplier Evidence File?

A Supplier Evidence File is a structured set of documents and records that supports buyer-facing claims. It can include legal identity, operational scope, product records, chain-of-custody evidence, origin data, emissions data, traceability files, contract clause support, audit trails, data governance and financial risk mapping.

When should a Brazilian supplier build a Supplier Evidence File?

Before the buyer escalates the request. Waiting for a questionnaire, contract schedule, audit notice, CBAM form, EUDR traceability request or bank due diligence process usually means responding under pressure. Evidence should be organized before the buyer controls the format and deadline.

What is buyer-ready evidence?

Buyer-ready evidence is documentation organized so that procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board teams can use it. It is not only a document folder. It is a structured file that connects each claim to proof, owner, source, update logic and commercial relevance.

What is board-usable evidence?

Board-usable evidence is supplier documentation structured for executive decision-making. It shows what is proven, what remains uncertain, which documents support the position, who owns the evidence, which risks remain and how those gaps can affect revenue, contracts, financing or market access.

How can weak evidence affect P&L?

Weak evidence can delay onboarding, increase legal review, trigger audit escalation, weaken pricing power, create discount pressure, reduce volume allocation, increase contract risk, damage renewal probability or weaken financing credibility. The cost may appear as friction before it appears as a formal sanction.

CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD and CSRD

Does CBAM apply directly to Brazilian suppliers?

The formal CBAM obligation generally sits with EU importers or indirect customs representatives, and the definitive CBAM regime has applied since 1 January 2026. Brazilian suppliers, however, may control the operational data the buyer needs, including product information, installation evidence, embedded emissions data, methodology support and documentation records.

What CBAM evidence may a European buyer request?

A buyer may request product specifications, material composition, CN-code logic, installation data, production-site records, emissions data, methodology support, carbon-price information, record retention logic, confidentiality controls and contractual cooperation evidence.

Does EUDR apply directly to Brazilian suppliers?

The formal EUDR due diligence obligation generally sits with EU operators or traders. The regulation applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium-sized operators and from 30 June 2027 for micro and small enterprises. Brazilian suppliers may control the origin, legality, geolocation, chain-of-custody and supplier records the buyer needs to build a defensible due diligence file.

What EUDR evidence may a European buyer request?

A buyer may request commodity scope, product-code relevance, origin records, geolocation evidence, legality records, deforestation-free support, custody documentation, supplier declarations, audit records and data-governance controls. A generic declaration may not be enough if the buyer needs a defensible file.

How do CSDDD and CSRD affect Brazilian suppliers?

CSDDD and CSRD generally regulate large European companies, not every Brazilian supplier directly. CSDDD, as amended by Directive (EU) 2026/470, is due for transposition by 26 July 2028 and applies from 26 July 2029. The commercial effect arrives earlier: large buyers may request supplier evidence to support due diligence, value-chain reporting, contract controls, risk assessment and board-level documentation.

Contracts, documents and response under pressure

Why do contract clauses matter for supplier evidence?

Contract clauses can convert regulatory pressure into supplier obligations. Warranties, audit rights, data duties, notification obligations, remediation duties, termination rights and indemnities may require proof. A supplier should not sign evidence obligations faster than the operation can defend the underlying facts.

What is contract clause evidence risk?

Contract clause evidence risk is the exposure created when a supplier accepts contractual obligations without having the documents, records, owners and audit trails needed to support them. It is an evidence problem that can become a financial problem.

What documents should a supplier prepare for EU buyer review?

Relevant documents may include buyer questionnaires, supplier agreements, product specifications, origin records, custody files, emissions data, audit reports, certificates, policies, supplier declarations, geolocation records, data-governance controls, contract clauses and internal ownership maps.

How should a supplier respond when the buyer asks for evidence quickly?

The supplier should avoid sending uncontrolled documents under pressure. First, identify what the buyer is asking, what risk the request relates to, which documents actually support the claim, what cannot yet be proven, what data should remain confidential and whether legal, technical or executive escalation is needed.

Can supplier evidence support financing discussions?

Yes, if it is structured correctly. Supplier evidence can support stronger conversations around revenue quality, operational controls, buyer-readiness, trade finance, supplier finance and Sustainability-Linked Loan preparation. It does not guarantee financing approval, pricing, KPI acceptance or lender validation.

Working with Villanova ESG

Is Villanova ESG a certification body?

No. Villanova ESG is an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory. It does not sell certification, buyer approval, audit assurance, customs clearance, emissions verification, legal opinion or regulatory clearance. The work focuses on evidence readiness, documentation gaps, buyer-readiness, contract risk and executive risk clarity.

What is the difference between the Supplier Evidence File Assessment and the EU Buyer Readiness Review?

The Supplier Evidence File Assessment reviews the supplier file itself: documents, records, owners, claims and gaps. The EU Buyer Readiness Review focuses on whether that file can survive the internal decision process of a European buyer across procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board review.

When should a supplier contact Villanova ESG?

A supplier should request triage when a European buyer asks for evidence, a contract includes ESG, CBAM, EUDR, due diligence or audit clauses, documentation is dispersed, emissions or traceability data is unclear, board materials require evidence, or a commercial deadline is approaching.

Which review fits the question?

The right review depends on the buyer request, the commercial deadline and the evidence domain under pressure.

Supplier Evidence File Assessment

Use when the supplier needs a full map of documents, gaps, buyer-readiness and regulatory exposure.

Is not: an audit, certification or legal opinion.

EU Buyer Readiness Review

Use when the supplier needs to understand whether the file can survive a European buyer’s internal review process.

Is not: an audit, certification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance.

Contract Clause Risk Review

Use when clauses, warranties, audit rights, data duties or indemnities require operational proof.

Is not: an audit, certification or legal opinion.

Move to the service pages when there is a live buyer request, contract clause, regulatory data demand, board review or commercial deadline: Supplier Evidence File Assessment, CBAM Evidence Review, EUDR Evidence Readiness Review, Contract Clause Risk Review, Board-Usable Evidence Review and EU Buyer Readiness Review. This page is a permanent index of the official regulatory sources Villanova ESG uses to structure EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory across CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, CSRD, ESRS and LGPD. Trust requires a visible source trail: executives, buyers, legal teams and retrieval systems should be able to check which official frameworks sit behind the advisory language before any of it enters a decision file.

Every external reference below points to an official institution — European Commission and EUR-Lex pages for EU law, ANPD for the Brazilian LGPD — grouped by regulatory evidence domain. The page is informational. It is not legal advice.

Why a source trail

Villanova ESG does not build supplier evidence advisory from generic ESG language. The advisory architecture is anchored in official legal instruments and guidance pages that shape buyer requests, contract clauses, customs workflows, reporting pressure, traceability demands and due diligence expectations. A single, stable source trail supports reference, verification and internal alignment.

Executive trust

CFOs, boards and legal teams need to know which official frameworks support the risk thesis before evidence is used in a decision file.

Buyer-readiness

European buyer requests are driven by customs, due diligence, reporting, contract and audit pressure. The source trail helps classify each demand against its origin.

AI-readable reference

A permanent, public source page reduces ambiguity for search engines and retrieval systems about the official references that define Villanova ESG's supplier evidence language.

From regulation to supplier evidence

Official sources do not create a supplier evidence file. They define the external pressure. Villanova ESG translates that pressure into documentation logic, buyer-readiness, contract defensibility and financial risk interpretation for Brazilian suppliers exposed to European buyers.

  1. The regulation defines the requirement. Official legal texts and Commission pages set dates, scope, obligations, implementation structures and supervision logic.
  2. The buyer translates it into requests. European buyers convert regulatory exposure into questionnaires, contract clauses, audit requests, portals and data demands.
  3. Supplier evidence answers it. Records, documents, data, owners, chain-of-custody logic and audit trails connect the operation to the buyer's risk decision.
The source trail is not the evidence file. A regulation tells the market what pressure exists. It does not tell a specific supplier which records, owners, clauses and controls a specific buyer will require. The advisory work begins where the official source meets the supplier's operating reality.

Official source index

The links below point to official institutions, regulatory pages or legal texts used as source anchors across Villanova ESG content and service pages.

CBAM · Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism

These sources support analysis of customs-linked emissions evidence: product classification, installation records, embedded emissions data, CBAM registry workflows, authorised declarant exposure and buyer-facing CBAM documentation. The CBAM definitive regime has applied since 1 January 2026.

  • European Commission · Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
  • European Commission · CBAM Registry and Reporting
  • European Commission · CBAM Legislation and Guidance
  • Regulation (EU) 2023/956 · Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
  • Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 · CBAM Simplification Amendments
  • European Commission · CBAM Questions and Answers

These sources frame CBAM evidence risk. They do not replace customs advice, legal review or technical emissions verification.

EUDR · Regulation on Deforestation-free Products

These sources support analysis of traceability evidence: commodity scope, origin proof, geolocation records, legality evidence, due diligence support and buyer-facing documentation for covered commodities and derived products. EUDR obligations apply from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and from 30 June 2027 for micro and small enterprises.

  • European Commission · Regulation on Deforestation-free Products
  • European Commission Green Forum · Implementing the EU Deforestation Regulation
  • European Commission Green Forum · Roles and Responsibilities under the EUDR
  • European Commission Green Forum · Understand Due Diligence
  • Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 · Deforestation-free Products
  • Regulation (EU) 2024/3234 · EUDR Amendment
  • Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 · EUDR Amendment

These sources frame traceability evidence risk. They do not replace legal advice, geospatial validation or deforestation-free certification.

CSDDD · Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence

These sources support analysis of due diligence pressure: buyer contractual controls, supplier evidence requests, adverse-impact evidence, remediation documentation and the transfer of due diligence expectations into supplier relationships. As amended by Directive (EU) 2026/470, transposition is due by 26 July 2028 and application starts on 26 July 2029.

  • European Commission · Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence
  • Directive (EU) 2024/1760 · Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive
  • Directive (EU) 2026/470 · Omnibus I Amendments to CSRD and CSDDD
  • Council of the EU · Simplification of Sustainability Reporting and Due Diligence Requirements

These sources frame buyer due diligence pressure. They do not replace legal counsel or jurisdiction-specific liability analysis.

CSRD and ESRS · Corporate Sustainability Reporting

These sources support analysis of value-chain reporting pressure: supplier data requests, sustainability information governance and board-usable evidence for reporting-related supplier inquiries.

  • European Commission · Corporate Sustainability Reporting
  • European Commission · CSRD Implementing and Delegated Acts
  • Directive (EU) 2022/2464 · Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive
  • Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 · European Sustainability Reporting Standards
  • European Commission · Feedback on Revised Sustainability Reporting Standards

These sources frame value-chain evidence pressure. They do not replace audit assurance, accounting advice or formal reporting counsel.

LGPD · Brazilian General Data Protection Law

These sources support analysis of data governance for supplier evidence: personal data, operational data, geolocation data, audit records, supplier information and buyer-facing document sharing.

  • ANPD · Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD), English version
  • ANPD · Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados

These sources frame evidence-sharing governance. They do not replace privacy counsel, data protection impact assessment or legal review.

Villanova ESG pages built on these sources

These pages translate official regulatory pressure into supplier evidence language, buyer-readiness logic and service scopes for Brazilian suppliers exposed to European buyers. They are commercial and informational; they do not replace the official sources above. Use them together when preparing supplier files, buyer responses, board materials, contract reviews, CBAM evidence, EUDR traceability evidence or EU buyer-readiness diagnostics.

  • EU–Brazil Supplier Evidence Knowledge Base
  • Supplier Evidence Glossary
  • FAQ: EU Buyer Evidence for Brazilian Suppliers
  • The 2026 EU Buyer Evidence File
  • Supplier Evidence File Assessment
  • CBAM Evidence Review for Brazilian Suppliers
  • EUDR Evidence Readiness Review
  • Contract Clause Risk Review for EU-Facing Suppliers
  • Board-Usable Evidence Review for EU-Facing Suppliers
  • EU Buyer Readiness Review for Brazilian Suppliers
  • The Firm — entity reference for Villanova ESG, Marcio Villanova and Ecobraz

Questions about this source trail

Is this page legal advice?

No. It is an informational source index listing the official sources Villanova ESG works from. It does not provide legal advice, legal interpretation, certification, audit assurance or regulatory clearance.

Why put official sources on one page?

Supplier evidence work needs traceable authority. A single source trail helps executives, buyers, legal teams, auditors, search engines and AI systems see which regulatory sources support the Villanova ESG evidence architecture.

Does listing a source mean a supplier is compliant?

No. A source identifies the regulatory framework. Compliance, buyer-readiness and evidence defensibility depend on the supplier's specific facts, documents, operations, contracts and buyer context.

How often should this page be reviewed?

Whenever CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, CSRD, ESRS, LGPD or related official guidance changes. Regulatory source pages change over time.

Can this page be cited in buyer or board materials?

It can be used as a source index. Specific legal, technical, customs, geospatial, reporting or audit claims should be supported by the applicable official source and, when required, specialist review.

How does this source trail support AI-readable search?

It provides a structured, public and indexable reference layer connecting Villanova ESG terminology, service pages and official regulatory sources. That reduces ambiguity for retrieval systems and generative search interfaces.

Official sources define the pressure. Evidence decides whether the buyer can rely on the file.

Brazilian suppliers exposed to European buyers need more than links to regulations — they need records, document owners and buyer-readable evidence connected to those sources.

title: Circular Supply Chain Evidence Toolkit for Non-EU Suppliers

html:
Circular operations can be technically valid at the facility level and still fail when presented to a European buyer. The failure point is rarely the activity itself. It is the absence of a structured evidence file that explains what happened, where it happened, who controlled the material, which records support the claim and what the buyer can reasonably rely on.

This public toolkit helps suppliers, buyers and circular-economy stakeholders organise proof of circular operations into a format that procurement, compliance, legal, finance and governance teams can read.

Public toolkit, version 1.0, July 2026. Publisher: Villanova ESG, an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory. Author: Marcio Villanova.

Who the toolkit serves

Suppliers

Identify whether circular activity is supported by records, custody logic, material-flow data and concise explanations that a buyer can review without reconstructing the process from scratch.

Buyers

Formulate evidence requests that are specific enough for procurement and compliance review, without demanding unnecessary documents from smaller or non-EU suppliers.

Circular-economy programmes

Use the model as a training structure for moving from circularity claims to practical documentation, especially in cross-border value chains involving secondary raw materials, electronics, industrial inputs or supplier services.

Four layers of circular evidence

The core question is not whether the supplier has a circularity narrative. The question is whether the evidence can be read, checked and used by the buyer.

Operational evidence

Records showing what process occurred: collection, sorting, reuse, refurbishment, treatment, recycling, recovery, disposal avoidance or other circular activity.

Chain-of-custody evidence

Records showing origin, transfer, custody holder, dates, locations, quantities, lots, responsible parties and destination.

Material-flow evidence

Records that connect input, process, output and destination, so that circularity indicators are not detached from actual material movement.

Buyer-readable evidence

A concise file that translates technical records into a structure usable by procurement, compliance, finance, legal and governance stakeholders.

The toolkit does not replace an audit, legal advice, certification or a regulatory determination. It is a practical evidence-organisation model.

Evidence readiness scorecard

The scorecard is intended for practical review. It does not certify performance. It identifies where evidence is absent, fragmented, structured or buyer-readable.

Evidence dimension0 · Absent1 · Fragmented2 · Structured3 · Buyer-readable
Operational proofNo reliable record of the activity.Activity is described, but records are informal or incomplete.Records identify process, date, location and responsible party.Records are indexed, consistent and explainable to a buyer.
Chain of custodyNo custody trail.Partial custody trail with gaps in transfer, timing or responsibility.Custody trail shows origin, transfer, responsible party and destination.Custody trail can be reconciled with material-flow and destination records.
Material flowNo input–output logic.Quantities are estimated or isolated from supporting records.Input, process, output and destination are documented.Material-flow records support circularity indicators and buyer review.
Circularity claimClaim without documentary basis.Claim supported by isolated evidence.Claim connected to process records and destination documents.Claim is limited, traceable and supported by a complete evidence file.
Buyer fileNo consolidated file.Documents exist but are dispersed across departments or suppliers.Documents are consolidated with index, scope and assumptions.File is concise, reviewable and usable for procurement and due diligence dialogue.

Why European buyers ask

In cross-border circular value chains, the non-EU supplier is not always the directly regulated entity. The European buyer, importer or reporting company may still request supplier evidence to support procurement screening, due diligence, product-data requirements, carbon data, traceability checks or sustainability reporting.

Procurement files

Buyers need structured supplier documentation before onboarding, renewal or contract expansion. Vague circularity claims are weak inputs for procurement decisions.

Due diligence files

Supplier information may be requested to support due diligence across operations, subsidiaries, chains of activities or value-chain relationships.

Product and material data

Circularity, recycled content, repairability, material origin and lifecycle information require records that can be linked to products, materials and processes.

Minimum evidence file for circular supply chain review

The index below is a practical structure. Adapt it to sector, product, material, risk profile and buyer request. Documents should be current, traceable to source records and consistent with the stated scope.

  • Scope note: product, material, service, facility, period and buyer request.
  • Supplier profile: legal entity, operational role and relevant sites.
  • Process map: collection, sorting, treatment, reuse, recycling, recovery or destination.
  • Licence and permit file: applicable operational and environmental documentation.
  • Chain-of-custody records: origin, transfer, custody holder, dates, quantities and destination.
  • Material-flow worksheet: input, output, losses, recovered material and final destination.
  • Destination evidence: certificates, receipts, treatment records or equivalent documents.
  • Circularity indicators: only when supported by matching records and defined boundaries.
  • Data-related records: where electronics, ICT assets or data-bearing devices are involved.
  • Assumptions and limitations note: what the evidence does and does not prove.
  • Document index: source, owner, date, version and link to the original file.
  • Executive evidence summary: a concise explanation for procurement, compliance and governance review.

The same structure underpins the buyer-readable evidence framework and the Supplier Evidence File Assessment.

How to apply the toolkit

Supplier questionnaires ask for final answers. Evidence work starts earlier. Before answering a buyer questionnaire, define the scope, map available records, separate supported claims from unsupported claims and prepare a reviewable explanation of the evidence base.

  1. Define the claim. Identify the exact circularity statement being made. Avoid broad claims such as “sustainable”, “zero impact” or “fully circular” unless the evidence supports the boundary and measurement logic.
  2. Map the records. List the documents that support the claim. Separate operational records, custody records, material-flow records, destination records and management statements.
  3. Test consistency. Check whether dates, quantities, locations, responsible parties and destinations are consistent across the evidence set. Resolve contradictions before buyer submission.
  4. Identify gaps. Classify each gap as missing, outdated, unverifiable, inconsistent, unclear, not buyer-readable or outside the defined scope.
  5. Prepare the file. Create a concise index, executive summary and limitation note. Do not send a raw document dump without explaining relevance and boundaries.
  6. Keep source records. The buyer-readable file is a summary layer. Source records must remain available for follow-up, clarification, audit or contractual review where applicable.

Regulatory context, not legal interpretation

This toolkit does not interpret legal obligations for specific companies. It uses EU policy and regulatory developments as context for why European buyers, importers and reporting companies request better supplier evidence.

  • EU circular economy. The EU describes the circular economy as keeping products and materials in circulation for as long as possible while minimising waste and resource use.
  • CBAM. The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism creates data pressure around embedded emissions for selected imported goods; the definitive regime applies since 1 January 2026.
  • EUDR. The EU Deforestation Regulation creates traceability and due diligence pressure for covered commodities and product groups; it applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and from 30 June 2027 for micro and small enterprises.
  • CSDDD. Corporate sustainability due diligence rules affect information flows across operations, subsidiaries and chains of activities. As amended by Directive (EU) 2026/470, Member States transpose by 26 July 2028 and application starts on 26 July 2029.
  • CSRD / ESRS. Sustainability reporting rules increase the need for consistent, structured information across companies and their value chains.
  • ESPR / Digital Product Passport. Product information, material origin, repair activities, recycling capabilities and lifecycle impacts are becoming more relevant to circular product policy.

Sources: EU circular economy strategy · CBAM · EUDR · CSDDD · CSRD · ESPR

What this toolkit is not

Evidence organisation improves clarity. It does not create facts that do not exist. It does not convert unsupported claims into verified outcomes. It does not replace regulatory, audit, customs, legal or certification procedures.

This toolkit does not provide certification, legal advice, customs advice, audit assurance, regulatory approval, buyer approval, bank approval, financing approval or a guarantee of compliance. It is a practical framework for organising supplier evidence, documentation gaps, circularity records and buyer-readable proof for more structured procurement, compliance and governance discussions. Questions about the methodology: contact@villanovaesg.com.

html:
European buyers rarely reject a supplier because the operation is wrong. They hesitate because the evidence file is unreadable. This framework organizes how a non-EU supplier translates operational circularity, traceability and environmental documentation into records a European procurement, compliance, legal or board-level team can review, question and escalate internally.

Villanova ESG is an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory. The framework is public. It describes evidence architecture, not communication claims.

The commercial failure point

A supplier may operate correctly, recycle materials, maintain licenses and retain records. That does not automatically mean the buyer can use those records inside procurement, compliance, sustainability reporting, legal review or board-level risk control.

What happens

European buyers request supplier questionnaires, traceability details, emissions inputs, origin information, disposal evidence or process records. The supplier answers with fragmented documents, generic ESG language or certificates that do not explain the operational logic.

Why it matters

Weak evidence creates buyer hesitation. Procurement delays onboarding. Legal asks for additional controls. Compliance escalates. Finance sees contract exposure. The issue becomes commercial before it becomes regulatory.

Six layers of buyer-usable evidence

The framework organizes supplier documentation around a single test: can the supplier explain what happened, who controlled it, where the records exist and how the evidence can be reviewed?

1. Operational evidence

Records showing the actual process: collection, sorting, dismantling, recovery, recycling, reuse, treatment, destruction or final destination. The question is not whether the activity is claimed. The question is whether it is documented.

2. Chain-of-custody evidence

Records connecting origin, movement, custody, date, responsible party, volume, batch, asset or material flow. This is where traceability becomes commercially defensible — or visibly weak.

3. Regulatory evidence

Licenses, registrations, permits, compliance files and environmental documents showing the operation can be explained under the applicable local and cross-border context.

4. Circularity evidence

Records of material recovery, waste avoidance, recycling, reuse, treatment or documented final destination. Circularity must be translated from narrative into records the buyer can test.

5. Buyer-readable evidence

Documentation structured for procurement, compliance, finance, legal and board review. The same file must make operational sense and commercial sense.

6. Risk translation

Evidence gaps mapped into procurement delay, contract friction, due-diligence escalation, revenue exposure and documentation priorities for the next buyer conversation.

How the pressure actually arrives

European regulation may not ask the Brazilian supplier directly. The European buyer often will — through questionnaires, supplier onboarding, contract clauses, product-data requests, traceability demands and due-diligence files. The sequence is predictable.

  1. Buyer request. The buyer asks for documentation linked to supplier risk, circularity, traceability, emissions, origin, due diligence or product data.
  2. Supplier response. The documents may be technically real but incomplete, scattered, unreconciled or commercially hard to interpret.
  3. Internal escalation. Procurement, compliance, legal or sustainability teams ask for clarification because the evidence does not support a clean internal decision.
  4. Commercial exposure. The problem becomes delay, renegotiation, supplier-replacement risk, contract friction or loss of confidence — long before it becomes a formal regulatory dispute.

The regulatory layer behind buyer questions

CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, CSRD and the Digital Product Passport are not the opening argument. They are the pressure layer behind buyer questions. The practical issue is whether supplier documentation can be reviewed, reconciled and used by the European counterparty.

CBAM: data gaps become buyer friction

The definitive CBAM regime applies since 1 January 2026. European importers of covered goods need emissions-related data, supplier cooperation and documentation discipline. See the CBAM Evidence Review.

EUDR: origin evidence becomes procurement pressure

EUDR applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 June 2027 for micro and small enterprises. Covered commodities and derived products require a stronger evidence logic around origin, traceability and deforestation-free claims. See the EUDR Evidence Readiness Review.

CSDDD, CSRD and DPP: structured proof gains value

CSDDD, as amended by Directive (EU) 2026/470, is due for transposition by 26 July 2028 and applies from 26 July 2029. Together with CSRD reporting and Digital Product Passport logic, it means buyers need supplier information they can integrate into due-diligence, reporting and product-data files without relying on generic ESG claims.

Evidence readiness scorecard

The scorecard is not a certification. It is a structured way to identify whether supplier evidence is absent, partial, organized or buyer-readable — before the buyer conversation becomes an escalation.

Evidence dimensionScore 0Score 1Score 2Score 3
Chain of custodyNo custody logic or disconnected records.Partial records exist but do not reconstruct the flow.Custody records are documented and internally coherent.Records are buyer-readable, reconciled and escalation-ready.
Material flowNo clear material or asset trail.Estimated or fragmented movement information.Material flow is recorded with dates, parties and volumes.Material flow can be reconciled against operational evidence.
Regulatory fileNo organized permits, licenses or compliance records.Basic records exist but are not indexed for buyer review.Documents are organized by operational relevance.Regulatory evidence is structured for procurement, legal and compliance review.
Circularity indicatorsOnly claims or marketing language.Isolated metrics without supporting records.Indicators are linked to process evidence.Indicators are supported by traceable, buyer-readable documentation.
Executive readabilityNo board-readable summary.Technical documents exist but require interpretation.Evidence summary exists for buyer-facing discussions.Documentation supports procurement, legal, compliance, CFO and board-level review.
Scores are a working diagnostic, not a rating, seal or guarantee of buyer acceptance.

What a supplier evidence file should organize

The buyer file does not need to be decorative. It needs to be legible, complete enough for the question asked and disciplined enough to reduce improvisation under pressure.

  1. Company and activity profile. Who operates, what is supplied, where the activity occurs and which buyer request is being answered.
  2. Licenses and registrations. Applicable permits, licenses, registrations and operational authorizations, indexed by relevance.
  3. Process map. The operational sequence showing how materials, products, assets or waste move through the chain.
  4. Chain-of-custody records. Documents connecting origin, dates, volumes, custody, responsible parties and destinations.
  5. Environmental documentation. Certificates, destination records, treatment records, recycling evidence and supporting documents.
  6. Data and asset controls. Where relevant, records showing asset handling, data destruction, security procedures and evidence retention.
  7. Risk statement. A concise explanation of what the evidence supports, where limitations remain and which records must not be overclaimed.
  8. Board-readable memo. A short executive file for procurement, legal, compliance, finance and board discussions.

What the review produces

Villanova ESG applies this framework in an advisory review of supplier evidence, documentation gaps and buyer-readiness questions. The objective is not ESG language. The objective is to reduce documentation improvisation.

Evidence gap map

A practical view of missing, weak, fragmented or unclear records that may trigger procurement or compliance escalation.

Is not: an audit or a compliance determination.

Buyer-readable structure

A documentation logic that translates operational proof into a file usable by European commercial and governance teams.

Is not: a certification, seal or regulatory approval.

Risk-priority memo

A concise executive view of what must be fixed, clarified, indexed or supported before the next buyer response.

Is not: a legal opinion or a guarantee of buyer acceptance.

Related: what Villanova ESG reviews · EU buyer readiness review for Brazilian suppliers · when a European buyer requests evidence.

The review is advisory. It is not an audit, certification or legal opinion, and it does not guarantee acceptance by any buyer, bank or regulator.

What this framework is not

Clear boundaries protect the file and the buyer conversation. The framework supports evidence organization and commercial defensibility. It does not replace regulated professional determinations or buyer decisions.

Not a certification

No supplier receives a certification, seal or regulatory approval from this framework.

Not buyer acceptance

No buyer approval, contract award or procurement acceptance is guaranteed.

Not legal or customs advice

Legal, customs, tax and formal regulatory determinations require the appropriate qualified professionals.

Not ESG marketing

The framework does not create generic sustainability claims. It organizes evidence for review.

Sources

Regulation is used here as the pressure layer behind buyer evidence requests. Review the official texts directly for legal interpretation.

The buyer does not evaluate the claim. The buyer evaluates the file. Villanova ESG — an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory — reviews whether supplier documentation can be read, challenged, organized and used by procurement, compliance, legal, finance and board-level stakeholders. The review targets claim-to-proof gaps, buyer-readability of documentation, traceability and chain-of-custody logic, and the commercial risk created by fragmented evidence.

Claims

Proof

Buyer

Risk

The weakness is the file, not the operation

Many Brazilian suppliers have real operations: legitimate procedures, licences, environmental records, logistics documentation and technical controls. The weakness is often not the operation. The weakness is the file.

European buyers increasingly need supplier documentation that works across procurement, compliance, legal, finance and governance functions. A fragmented file creates ambiguity. Ambiguity triggers questions. Questions delay decisions. Delays create commercial exposure.

The market is moving from ESG storytelling to evidence discipline. A supplier must be able to show what happened, how it was documented, who can verify each link in the chain, where the gaps sit and whether the file survives a serious buyer review.

Founder position. Evidence is no longer a back-office archive. It is market-access infrastructure. Marcio Villanova's work connects Brazilian operational proof with documentation European buyers can read.

Where evidence usually fails

A supplier can be operationally strong and still commercially exposed. Buyer hesitation rarely starts with a public claim. It starts when the documentation cannot answer the next question.

Fragmented records

Documents exist, but they are dispersed across departments, vendors, spreadsheets, certificates, invoices, declarations and emails. The buyer sees operational noise, not reviewable evidence.

Non-buyer-readable files

The supplier has documentation, but it is not structured for procurement, legal, compliance or finance review. The file answers internal questions, not buyer questions.

Weak traceability logic

Chain-of-custody, origin, waste-stream, transport, treatment, carbon or product-data logic may be incomplete. The weakness is not always a missing document. It is often a missing connection.

Pressure transmitted by buyers

European regulation may not ask the Brazilian supplier directly. The European buyer often will, through questionnaires, clauses, onboarding files and documentation requests.

Finance-readiness weakness

Operational performance does not automatically become financing credibility. Banks and lenders need structured evidence, not only environmental language.

Evidence quality is a financial control issue

Weak supplier evidence slows procurement decisions, increases legal review, damages buyer confidence and weakens capital conversations. The file is not administrative detail. It is part of revenue protection. The exposure typically builds in four steps:

  1. Buyer request. A European buyer asks for supplier evidence: traceability, emissions data, origin documentation, waste records, operational proof or due diligence files.

Regulation arrives as procurement pressure

CSDDD, CBAM, EUDR, CSRD and Scope 3 expectations matter to a Brazilian supplier because they shape the questions European buyers, lenders and governance functions ask.

Finance

html:
La due diligence europea entra nei vostri contratti di fornitura come testo contrattuale: garanzie, diritti di audit, obblighi di dati, allegati con codici di condotta. La clausola protegge solo se il fornitore può provare ciò che firma — altrimenti avete trasferito il rischio sulla carta, ma non nella realtà: alla prima verifica, il problema torna da voi.

Lavoro consulenziale — evidenza contro clausola. Non è consulenza legale, audit né certificazione; il vostro legale resta il vostro legale.

Dove si nasconde il rischio

Garanzie senza archivio

“Il fornitore garantisce la conformità a…” — firmata senza un registro di quali evidenze sostengono ogni affermazione garantita.

Audit senza controllo

Diritti di accesso concessi in modo ampio, senza governance documentale: che cosa esiste, dove, chi risponde.

Dati senza limiti

Obblighi continui di dati che il fornitore non può adempiere — o che espongono dettagli industriali senza controlli di riservatezza.

Che cosa copre la revisione

  1. Mappa clausola per clausola. Che cosa chiede davvero ogni clausola in termini di evidenza — due diligence, reporting, cooperazione, conservazione, responsabilità.
  2. Confronto con l’evidenza. I record del fornitore contro ogni richiesta: sostenuta, parzialmente sostenuta, non sostenuta.
  3. Lettura del trasferimento di rischio. Quali clausole restano promesse di carta — e quali proteggono davvero.
  4. File di supporto alla negoziazione. Che cosa esigere, che cosa delimitare, che cosa far evidenziare prima — in linguaggio che acquisti e legale condividono.
  5. Registro delle lacune. Responsabili e date — graduato sul framework SEMM.

Un esempio concreto

Un’azienda della pelletteria rinnova il contratto con un fornitore brasiliano di cuoio, aggiungendo l’allegato di due diligence: garanzie socio-ambientali, audit “con preavviso ragionevole”, dati “su richiesta”. Se il fornitore firma senza poter provare, la clausola vale poco proprio quando serve. Sapere prima della firma che cosa è provabile — e che cosa va evidenziato — è ciò che questa revisione prepara.

Le domande che riceviamo per prime

È consulenza legale?

No. Il vostro legale scrive e negozia il contratto. Noi produciamo la lettura di evidenza — che cosa il fornitore può provare — che rende solida la posizione del vostro legale.

La CSDDD non è ancora definitiva — perché ora?

Perché le clausole sono già nei contratti. L’obbligo commerciale arriva con la firma, non con il calendario di recepimento.

Quanto costa?

Caso per caso, con proposta scritta — volume contrattuale e complessità dell’evidenza determinano il lavoro. Nessun listino, per scelta.

Un contratto in firma? Inviate la clausola così com’è — rispondiamo con i rischi prioritari entro 1 giorno lavorativo.

Inizia la valutazione →

Esposizione più ampia di un contratto? Vedi l'analisi completa dei fornitori.

html:
Per i grandi operatori l’EUDR si applica dal 30 dicembre 2026 — e la prova che la legge chiede a voi sta nei lotti brasiliani: caffè, cacao, soia, carne, cuoio, legno, gomma e derivati. Il punto debole raramente è la commodity. È la catena di evidenze dietro origine, legalità e due diligence — scritta in portoghese, sparsa tra cooperative, esportatori e spedizionieri.

Revisione consulenziale. Non è audit, certificazione, parere legale né garanzia di conformità.

Tre modi in cui l’evidenza di origine fallisce

Dichiarata, non geolocalizzata

L’origine è dichiarata, ma non si collega a coordinate utilizzabili, dati per appezzamento o un dossier tracciabile.

Tracciata, non valutata

I dati esistono, ma senza una valutazione del rischio difendibile né un record di due diligence strutturato per la vostra revisione.

Rilevante, non utilizzabile

L’evidenza incide sull’accesso al mercato, ma non è in un formato che i vostri uffici possano usare.

Che cosa copre la revisione

  1. Perimetro di commodity e prodotto. Quali flussi dei vostri fornitori rientrano nelle categorie EUDR.
  2. Geolocalizzazione e origine. Dati per appezzamento e collegamento tra dichiarazioni e file verificabili.
  3. Record di legalità. La catena documentale dietro ogni affermazione, letta come la legge la richiede.
  4. Struttura di due diligence. Logica di valutazione del rischio, mitigazione e controlli sulla condivisione dei dati.
  5. Registro delle lacune. Responsabili, date e fonti — graduato sul framework SEMM.

Un esempio concreto

Una torrefazione compra caffè dal Sud di Minas attraverso una cooperativa. La struttura è reale, l’origine è legittima — ma dichiarazioni, appezzamenti e record di custodia stanno in mani diverse. Che il rinnovo regga o salti lo decide la catena di evidenze, non il caffè. Collegarla — appezzamento, custodia, legalità, dichiarazione — è ciò che questa revisione struttura.

Le domande che riceviamo per prime

Le certificazioni non bastano?

Aiutano, ma l’EUDR chiede evidenza specifica: geolocalizzazione, legalità e due diligence in una catena utilizzabile. Un certificato scollegato dai lotti non risponde al sistema informativo.

È presto per muoversi?

Costruire la catena sotto scadenza è la versione costosa dello stesso lavoro. I compratori più strutturati stanno chiedendo adesso.

Quanto costa?

Caso per caso, con proposta scritta — perimetro di commodity e complessità della filiera determinano il lavoro. Nessun listino, per scelta.

Avete una filiera EUDR da mappare? Descrivetela — rispondiamo con le opzioni di perimetro entro 1 giorno lavorativo.

html:
Il regime definitivo del CBAM si applica dal 1º gennaio 2026 (come modificato dal Regolamento (UE) 2025/2083). L’obbligo formale è dell’importatore europeo — cioè vostro. Ma i fatti operativi che vi servono stanno in Brasile: classificazione dei prodotti, dati di impianto, emissioni incorporate. Se il fornitore non li prova, pagate i valori di default — e la differenza esce dal margine.

Lavoro consulenziale. Non è audit, certificazione, parere legale né verifica delle emissioni.

Dove il CBAM tocca il conto economico

Valori di default

Senza dati reali del fornitore, l’esposizione si calcola con assunzioni conservative — quasi sempre peggiori della realtà brasiliana.

File doganale

Il vostro dichiarante CBAM ha bisogno di un file difendibile: prodotto, impianto, metodologia, prezzo del carbonio pagato all’origine.

Rinegoziazione

Chi può modellare il costo del carbonio prima della trattativa, negozia. Chi non può, subisce.

Che cosa copre la revisione

  1. Perimetro di prodotto. Codici NC, flussi coperti e materialità — prima che le assunzioni diventino obblighi.
  2. Evidenza di impianto. I record che collegano il prodotto al sito produttivo e ai suoi dati.
  3. Logica delle emissioni incorporate. Fonti, metodologia e documentazione che il vostro dichiarante può difendere.
  4. Controlli contrattuali. Accuratezza dei dati, diritti di audit e riservatezza nei contratti con i fornitori.
  5. Registro delle lacune. Che cosa esiste, che cosa manca, chi risponde — graduato sul framework SEMM.

Un esempio concreto

Un centro servizi acciaio importa laminati brasiliani. Il fornitore ha i dati — in cinque fogli di calcolo, due sistemi e la relazione di un consulente. Quello che arriva al vostro dichiarante decide se l’importazione parte dall’evidenza o dai valori di default con sconto. Quella traduzione è esattamente ciò che questa revisione produce.

Le domande che riceviamo per prime

Verificate le emissioni?

No. La verifica delle emissioni è un’attività accreditata. Verifichiamo se l’evidenza del fornitore reggerebbe l’esame — e dove no.

Il fornitore collaborerà?

Il lavoro avviene in portoghese, all’origine, con un registro delle lacune che il fornitore può eseguire. La collaborazione migliora quando la richiesta diventa comprensibile.

Quanto costa?

Caso per caso, con proposta scritta — perimetro di prodotto e dispersione dei record determinano la profondità. Nessun listino, per scelta.

Avete una scadenza CBAM? Inviate la richiesta così com’è — rispondiamo con i rischi prioritari entro 1 giorno lavorativo.

I questionari che inviate tornano — in portoghese, in ritardo, non comparabili e impossibili da valutare da Milano o Torino. Noi lavoriamo l’altro capo del problema: all’origine.

Lavoro consulenziale. Non è audit, certificazione, parere legale, verifica delle emissioni né garanzia — e ogni deliverable dichiara questo limite.

Che cosa facciamo per i compratori

Valutazione per fornitore

Ogni fornitore graduato sul framework SEMM pubblicato: che cosa esiste, che cosa manca, che cosa non supererebbe la vostra revisione — con responsabile, data, perimetro e fonte per ogni voce. Comparabile su tutta la base fornitori.

Coorte pilota

Si parte da un gruppo ristretto di fornitori critici — quanto basta per testare il metodo sul vostro framework prima di estenderlo. Perimetro, coorte e calendario definiti nella conversazione iniziale.

Percorso di sviluppo

La valutazione senza percorso genera attrito. Ogni fornitore graduato riceve un registro delle lacune con priorità, in portoghese — così la vostra base fornitori migliora invece di ruotare.

Perché all'origine — e perché noi

  1. Lingua e realtà sul campo. L’evidenza brasiliana è scritta in portoghese e riferita a strumenti brasiliani (MTR, CDF, licenze). Leggerla correttamente è il lavoro — la sola traduzione perde perimetro e riserve.
  2. Un metro pubblicato. La metodologia è pubblica, citabile e depositata con DOI — i vostri comitati possono leggere esattamente come nasce ogni valutazione. Nessun punteggio a scatola nera.
  3. Esperienza operativa reale. Il fondatore guida dal 2011 un’operazione brasiliana documentata di logistica inversa. Organizzazioni distinte, relazione dichiarata: chi valuta una catena di custodia ne ha gestita una.
  4. Disciplina dei limiti. Ogni deliverable dichiara che cosa ogni record prova e che cosa non prova. Se un’affermazione non è verificabile, non viene scritta.

Il deliverable: un dossier per fornitore che i vostri uffici acquisti, legale e compliance possono usare senza ricostruire nulla — graduato SEMM, con registro delle lacune e priorità di intervento.

Le domande che riceviamo per prime

Potete certificare i nostri fornitori?

No — e diffidate di chi dice di sì. Produciamo valutazioni consulenziali con metodologia pubblicata. La certificazione è un’attività accreditata, diversa.

Lavorate in italiano?

I deliverable sono in italiano o inglese, a vostra scelta; il lavoro all’origine avviene in portoghese — è esattamente il punto.

Quanto costa?

Ogni incarico è definito caso per caso — dimensione della coorte, profondità e calendario. La conversazione iniziale si chiude con una proposta scritta. Nessun listino, per scelta.

html:
As obrigações europeias de cadeia de valor terminam em lugares como São Paulo: o galpão do fornecedor, o descarte dos ativos de TI, a documentação do que de fato aconteceu com os materiais. O Programa Escopo 3 Brasil existe para empresas que precisam dessa ponta brasileira documentada na origem — não estimada de uma mesa na Europa.

Trabalho consultivo. Não é auditoria, certificação, parecer jurídico, verificação de emissões nem garantia de aceitação — e todo entregável declara esse limite.

Como o programa é construído

  1. Estruturação. Definição de escopo, mapeamento do trecho brasileiro da cadeia, arquitetura de evidências e dossiê-base — graduado no framework SEMM.
  2. Doze meses de acompanhamento. O dossiê mantido com a operação rodando: registros coletados na origem, lacunas registradas e fechadas, visibilidade mensal.
  3. Relatório anual do programa. O que foi executado, o que está documentado, o que cada registro prova e o que não prova — escrito para os seus comitês e, quando você quiser, para o seu verificador independente.

Por que na origem

Estimativa envelhece

Estimativa de mesa envelhece no momento em que a operação muda. Registro coletado na origem, quando o evento acontece, não precisa de reconstrução um ano depois.

Comprador pede prova

O reporte de cadeia de valor encontra o setor de compras: o mesmo dossiê responde o pedido de dados CSRD e o questionário do comprador.

Terceiros podem verificar

O programa nasce de portas abertas: cada registro com dono, data, escopo e fonte, para verificação independente testar — essa abertura é o objetivo.

Quem faz o quê — relação declarada

A Villanova ESG assessora e documenta. A Ecobraz opera. A Ecobraz é uma organização brasileira de logística reversa (coleta, triagem, destinação documentada de eletrônicos, clientes corporativos desde 2011), fundada e dirigida pelo mesmo principal da Villanova ESG. Declaramos a relação em vez de escondê-la; nenhuma organização certifica a outra, e revisões que toquem evidência da Ecobraz são declaradas como parte relacionada.

O que perguntam primeiro

Isso é contabilidade de carbono?

Não. O programa documenta a camada de evidência — o que aconteceu, com quais registros — que a sua contabilidade de carbono e a sua verificação usam depois. Verificação de emissões segue sendo atividade acreditada.

Nosso verificador pode confiar nisso?

Ele testa — esse é o papel dele. O trabalho do programa é que, quando testar, os registros estejam localizáveis, com dono, com data e coerentes.

Quanto custa?

Escopo anual, caso a caso, com proposta por escrito — a complexidade do trecho da cadeia define o trabalho. Sem tabela de preço, de propósito.

Precisa da ponta brasileira documentada? Descreva o trecho — respondemos com opções de escopo em 1 dia útil.

Começar a conversa de escopo →

html:
Um dossiê organizado uma vez começa a decair no dia da entrega: licenças vencem, fornecedores mudam, chega um questionário novo com perguntas diferentes. A Gestão Contínua de Evidências é o acompanhamento que mantém o dossiê no nível 4 do SEMM — gerido continuamente — em vez de deixar cada pedido de comprador reiniciar a arqueologia.

Trabalho consultivo. Não é auditoria, certificação, parecer jurídico, verificação de emissões nem garantia de aceitação — e todo entregável declara esse limite.

O que é gerido, mês a mês

Validade e vencimento

Cada registro datado rastreado; renovações sinalizadas antes de virarem lacuna que o comprador acha primeiro.

Calendário de atualização

Registro do que mudou na operação e quais documentos precisam acompanhar — com donos e datas.

Suporte a pedidos

Quando chega questionário, cláusula ou pedido de dados, a resposta sai da estrutura mantida — revisada, com escopo, no prazo do comprador.

Re-graduação periódica

O dossiê re-graduado no SEMM em intervalos combinados — melhora (ou decadência) visível e atribuível.

A economia do nível 4

  1. Dossiê nível 1–2: cada pedido é um projeto — dias de reconstrução e desconto concedido sob pressão de prazo.
  2. Dossiê nível 3: pedidos são respondíveis — mas o dossiê decai sem manutenção e desliza de volta em silêncio.
  3. Dossiê nível 4: pedidos são exportações. O custo é um acompanhamento previsível em vez de emergências imprevisíveis — e o comprador nota a diferença no tempo de resposta.

O que perguntam primeiro

Precisamos de uma revisão antes?

Normalmente sim — o acompanhamento mantém um dossiê estruturado. A Revisão de Evidências constrói a estrutura; isto a mantém viva.

Em quais formatos existe?

Anual, em três cadências — do ritmo essencial para dossiês estáveis ao acompanhamento próximo para cadeias sob pressão ativa. Caso a caso, com proposta por escrito.

Cobre vários fornecedores?

Sim — programas do lado do comprador mantêm dossiês graduados de uma carteira de fornecedores; veja para compradores europeus.

Cansado da arqueologia? Conte onde o dossiê está — respondemos com a cadência recomendada em 1 dia útil.

Se a sua empresa compra do Brasil, as regras europeias transferiram, silenciosamente, a papelada dos seus fornecedores para a sua mesa: deveres de due diligence sob a CSDDD, relato de cadeia de valor sob a CSRD, dados de emissões incorporadas sob o CBAM, rastreabilidade sob o EUDR. Os questionários que você envia voltam — em português, atrasados, incomparáveis e impossíveis de avaliar de Munique ou de Milão.

A Villanova ESG trabalha a outra ponta desse problema: na origem. Revisamos a evidência dos seus fornecedores brasileiros onde ela vive — no idioma em que foi escrita, contra a operação que descreve — e a devolvemos na estrutura que os seus times de compras, compliance e auditoria conseguem de fato usar.

É um trabalho de advisory. Não é auditoria, certificação, parecer jurídico, verificação de emissões nem garantia de aceitação pelo comprador — e todo entregável declara esse limite.

O que fazemos para compradores

Avaliação de evidências por fornecedor

Cada fornecedor avaliado contra o framework publicado SEMM: o que existe, o que falta, o que não sobreviveria à sua revisão — com responsável, data, escopo e fonte por registro. Comparável em toda a base de fornecedores.

Não é: auditoria, nota autodeclarada ao estilo EcoVadis, nem certificação de instalação.

Coorte-piloto

Comece com um conjunto pequeno de fornecedores críticos — o suficiente para testar o método contra o seu framework antes de estendê-lo à base inteira. Escopo, coorte e calendário definidos na conversa de escopo.

Trilha de desenvolvimento de fornecedores

Avaliação sem caminho gera ressentimento. Cada fornecedor avaliado recebe um registro de lacunas priorizado, em português — para que a sua base de fornecimento melhore em vez de rodar.

Por que na origem — e por que nós

  1. Idioma e realidade de campo. A evidência brasileira é escrita em português e referenciada a instrumentos brasileiros (MTR, CDF, licenças). Lê-la com precisão é o próprio trabalho — a tradução, sozinha, perde o escopo e as ressalvas.
  2. Uma régua publicada. A metodologia é pública, citável e depositada com DOIs — os seus comitês podem ler exatamente como cada nota foi produzida. Nada de pontuação em caixa-preta.
  3. Linhagem operacional. O fundador também lidera a Ecobraz, uma operação brasileira de logística reversa documentada, que atende clientes corporativos desde 2011. Organizações distintas, relação declarada: significa que quem avalia um registro de cadeia de custódia já operou uma.
  4. Disciplina de limites. Os entregáveis declaram o que cada registro prova e o que não prova. Se uma afirmação não pode ser verificada, ela não é escrita.

Onde isso se encaixa nas suas obrigações

As avaliações são desenhadas para alimentar os processos que as regras exigem de você — análise de risco e monitoramento sob a CSDDD, informações de cadeia de valor para a CSRD, organização de dados de fornecedores para CBAM e EUDR — sem a pretensão de substituí-los. O seu dever legal, o seu provedor de asseguração e os seus relatórios continuam sendo seus; o nosso trabalho torna a evidência subjacente dos fornecedores utilizável dentro deles.

O que os compradores nos perguntam primeiro

Vocês podem certificar nossos fornecedores? Não — e desconfie de quem disser que sim. Produzimos avaliações de advisory com metodologia publicada. Certificação é uma atividade distinta, acreditada.

Vocês trabalham em inglês? Os entregáveis são em inglês (ou em italiano, sob demanda); o trabalho na origem acontece em português — esse é justamente o ponto.

Quanto custa? Os engajamentos têm escopo definido caso a caso — tamanho da coorte, profundidade e calendário dimensionam o trabalho. A conversa de escopo termina com uma proposta por escrito.

html:
Todo trabalho da Villanova ESG é graduado numa régua publicada: o Modelo de Maturidade de Evidências de Fornecedores (SEMM). Ele responde a pergunta que decide contratos nas cadeias UE–Brasil: a que distância a evidência deste fornecedor está de ser usada na decisão de um comprador europeu?

Trabalho consultivo. Não é auditoria, certificação, parecer jurídico, verificação de emissões nem garantia de aceitação pelo comprador — e todo entregável declara esse limite.

Por que um modelo de maturidade — e não um checklist

Checklist pergunta se o documento existe. Comprador, banco e regulador perguntam algo mais difícil: se o registro sobreviveria à análise deles — atual, com escopo, com dono, coerente com a operação e legível por quem não estava na sala. O SEMM gradua essa distância, para fornecedor, comprador e consultor falarem do mesmo dossiê com as mesmas palavras.

Os cinco níveis

Nível 0 — Inexistente

A evidência que o pedido exige não existe, ou não é encontrada. A resposta ao comprador seria o silêncio.

Nível 1 — Fragmentada

Registros existem, mas espalhados em caixas de e-mail, planilhas e fornecedores de fornecedores. Reconstruir uma resposta é um projeto toda vez.

Nível 2 — Organizada

Registros coletados e arquivados, mas não mapeados às perguntas que os compradores realmente fazem — completude sem legibilidade.

Nível 3 — Pronta para decisão

Cada pergunta provável do comprador ligada ao registro que a responde, com dono, data, escopo e fonte. Um CFO defende o dossiê em uma reunião.

Nível 4 — Gerida continuamente

O dossiê é um ativo vivo: controle de validade, calendário de atualização e registro do que mudou e por quê. O próximo pedido é exportação, não emergência.

Público e citável. A definição oficial — dimensões, critérios de graduação e exemplos trabalhados — está depositada com DOI no Zenodo, ao lado de 18 relatórios técnicos. Seus comitês podem ler exatamente como uma nota foi produzida. Sem caixa-preta.

Como o SEMM é usado

  1. Em toda revisão. A Revisão de Evidências e as trilhas CBAM, EUDR, cláusulas e dados de produto entregam dossiê graduado no SEMM.
  2. Por compradores. Equipes de compras europeias usam os níveis para comparar fornecedores na mesma escala — veja para compradores europeus.
  3. Pela sua própria equipe. Pontue-se primeiro com os materiais executivos abaixo.

O que perguntam primeiro

Nota SEMM é certificação?

Não. É graduação consultiva com metodologia publicada — comparável e defensável, mas não é certificação acreditada nem garantia de aceitação.

Podemos usar o SEMM internamente sem contratar?

Sim — o modelo é público e citável. O whitepaper explica níveis e critérios; muitas equipes se autoavaliam antes de decidir se uma revisão vale o investimento.

Onde a maioria dos fornecedores está?

Nos nossos trabalhos até aqui, a maioria entra entre os níveis 1 e 2 — registros reais, legibilidade fraca. O salto comercial é do 2 para o 3.

Quer seu dossiê graduado? Envie o pedido de comprador que você recebeu — respondemos com os riscos prioritários e o próximo passo, em 1 dia útil.

Começar a triagem →

Leia o modelo: o whitepaper SEMM (PDF, mediante cadastro) · ou autoavalie com o Checklist do CFO e a Matriz de Prontidão.

European value-chain obligations end in places like São Paulo: the supplier's warehouse, the disposal of IT assets, the documentation of what actually happened to materials. The Scope 3 Brazil Programme exists for companies that need that Brazilian end documented at source — not estimated from a desk in Europe.

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

How the programme is built

  1. Setup. Scope definition, mapping of the Brazilian chain segment, evidence architecture and a baseline file — graded against the SEMM framework.
  2. Twelve months of accompaniment. The evidence file maintained as the operation runs: records collected at origin, gaps registered and closed, monthly visibility.
  3. Annual programme report. What was executed, what is documented, what each record proves and what it does not — written to be read by your committees and, when you choose, by your independent assurance provider.

Why at source

Estimates decay

Desk estimates age the moment the operation changes. Records collected at origin, as events happen, do not need reconstruction a year later.

Buyers ask for proof

Value-chain reporting increasingly meets procurement: the same file answers the CSRD data request and the buyer questionnaire.

Third parties can verify

The programme is built with open doors: every record carries owner, date, scope and source, so independent assurance can test it — that openness is the point.

Who does what — a declared relationship

Villanova ESG advises and documents. Ecobraz operates. Ecobraz is a Brazilian reverse-logistics organisation (collection, sorting, documented disposal of electronics, serving corporate clients since 2011), founded and led by the same principal as Villanova ESG. We state this relationship rather than hide it; neither organisation certifies the other, and reviews touching Ecobraz evidence are disclosed as related-party work.

Is this carbon accounting?

No. The programme documents the evidence layer — what happened, with which records — that your carbon accounting and assurance then use. Emissions verification remains an accredited activity.

Can our assurance provider rely on it?

They test it — that is their role. The programme's job is that when they do, the records are findable, owned, dated and consistent.

What does it cost?

Annual scope, case by case, with a written proposal — driven by chain-segment complexity. No price list, by design.
